def and_masks(*mask_functions: Callable) -> Callable:
    """Returns a mask function that is the intersection of provided mask functions"""
    if not all(callable(arg) for arg in mask_functions):
        raise RuntimeError(f"All inputs should be callable mask_functions: {mask_functions}")

    def and_mask(batch_idx, head_idx, q_idx, kv_idx):
        result = q_idx.new_ones((), dtype=torch.bool)
        for mask in mask_functions:
            result = result & mask(batch_idx, head_idx, q_idx, kv_idx).to(result.device)
        return result

    return and_mask


def or_masks(*mask_functions: Callable) -> Callable:
    """Returns a mask function that is the union of provided mask functions"""
    if not all(callable(arg) for arg in mask_functions):
        raise RuntimeError(f"All inputs should be callable mask_functions: {mask_functions}")

    def or_mask(batch_idx, head_idx, q_idx, kv_idx):
        result = q_idx.new_zeros((), dtype=torch.bool)
        for mask in mask_functions:
            result = result | mask(batch_idx, head_idx, q_idx, kv_idx).to(result.device)
        return result

    return or_mask


def causal_mask_function(batch_idx: int, head_idx: int, q_idx: int, kv_idx: int) -> bool:
    """
    This creates a basic lower-diagonal causal mask.
    """
    return kv_idx <= q_idx


def bidirectional_mask_function(batch_idx: int, head_idx: int, q_idx: int, kv_idx: int) -> bool:
    """
    This creates a full bidirectional mask.

    NOTE: It is important to keep an index-based version for non-vmap expansion.
    """
    return q_idx >= 0


def sliding_window_overlay(sliding_window: int) -> Callable:
    """
    This is an overlay depicting a sliding window pattern. Add it on top of a causal mask for a proper sliding
    window mask.
    """

    def inner_mask(batch_idx: int, head_idx: int, q_idx: int, kv_idx: int) -> bool:
        return kv_idx > q_idx - sliding_window

    return inner_mask


def chunked_overlay(chunk_size: int, left_padding: torch.Tensor) -> Callable:
    """
    This is an overlay depicting a chunked attention pattern. Add it on top of a causal mask for a proper chunked
    attention mask.
    """

    def inner_mask(batch_idx: int, head_idx: int, q_idx: int, kv_idx: int) -> bool:
        return (kv_idx - left_padding[batch_idx]) // chunk_size == (q_idx - left_padding[batch_idx]) // chunk_size

    return inner_mask


def blockwise_overlay(block_sequence_ids: torch.Tensor) -> Callable:
    """
    This is an overlay depicting a blockwise masking pattern. Instead of a single
    token, each block consists of arbitrary length tokens. In causal setup, each block
    can attend to prev block causally and can't attend to future blocks. Within one block
    the attention is always bidirectional.
    Mostly used in MLLMs when non-text data attends bidirectionally to itself.
    """

    def inner_mask(batch_idx: int, head_idx: int, q_idx: int, kv_idx: int) -> bool:
        # Unmask if the q and kv come from same group which is not -1 (i.e. non-text)
        q_group = block_sequence_ids[batch_idx, q_idx]
        kv_group = block_sequence_ids[batch_idx, kv_idx]
        return (q_group == kv_group) & (q_group >= 0)

    return inner_mask


def sliding_window_causal_mask_function(sliding_window: int) -> Callable:
    """
    This return the mask_function function to create a sliding window mask.
    """
    return and_masks(sliding_window_overlay(sliding_window), causal_mask_function)


def sliding_window_bidirectional_overlay(sliding_window: int) -> Callable:
    """
    This is an overlay depicting a bidirectional sliding window pattern.
    """

    def inner_mask(batch_idx: int, head_idx: int, q_idx: int, kv_idx: int) -> bool:
        """A token can attend to any other token if their absolute distance is within
        the (inclusive) sliding window size (distance <= sliding_window)."""
        return abs(q_idx - kv_idx) <= sliding_window

    return inner_mask


def sliding_window_bidirectional_mask_function(sliding_window: int) -> Callable:
    """
    This return the mask_function function to create a bidirectional sliding window mask.
    """
    return and_masks(sliding_window_bidirectional_overlay(sliding_window), bidirectional_mask_function)


def chunked_causal_mask_function(chunk_size: int, left_padding: torch.Tensor) -> Callable:
    """
    This return the mask_function function to create a chunked attention mask.
    """
    return and_masks(chunked_overlay(chunk_size, left_padding), causal_mask_function)


def padding_mask_function(padding_mask: torch.Tensor) -> Callable:
    """
    This return the mask_function function corresponding to a 2D padding mask.
    """

    def inner_mask(batch_idx: int, head_idx: int, q_idx: int, kv_idx: int) -> bool:
        # Note that here the mask should ALWAYS be at least of the max `kv_index` size in the dimension 1. This is because
        # we cannot pad it here in the mask_function as we don't know the final size, and we cannot try/except, as it is not
        # vectorizable on accelerator devices
        return padding_mask[batch_idx, kv_idx]

    return inner_mask


def packed_sequence_mask_function(packed_sequence_mask: torch.Tensor) -> Callable:
    """
    This return the mask_function function corresponding to a 2D packed sequence mask.
    """

    def inner_mask(batch_idx: int, head_idx: int, q_idx: int, kv_idx: int) -> bool:
        return packed_sequence_mask[batch_idx, q_idx] == packed_sequence_mask[batch_idx, kv_idx]

    return inner_mask


def add_offsets_to_mask_function(mask_function: Callable, q_offset: int, kv_offset: int) -> Callable:
    """
    This function adds the correct offsets to the `q_idx` and `kv_idx` as the torch API can only accept lengths,
    not start and end indices.
    """

    def inner_mask(batch_idx: int, head_idx: int, q_idx: int, kv_idx: int) -> bool:
        return mask_function(batch_idx, head_idx, q_idx + q_offset, kv_idx + kv_offset)

    return inner_mask


def prepare_padding_mask(attention_mask: torch.Tensor | None, kv_length: int, kv_offset: int) -> torch.Tensor | None:
    """
    From the 2D attention mask, prepare the correct padding mask to use by potentially padding it.
    """
    local_padding_mask = attention_mask
    if attention_mask is not None:
        # Pad it if necessary
        if (padding_length := kv_length + kv_offset - attention_mask.shape[-1]) > 0:
            local_padding_mask = torch.nn.functional.pad(attention_mask, (0, padding_length))
    return local_padding_mask


def maybe_pad_block_sequence_ids(
    block_sequence_ids: torch.Tensor, attention_mask: torch.Tensor | None, kv_length: int, kv_offset: int
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """
    Pads the `block_sequence_ids` in case the total length is less than `kv_length`.
    Usually that happens with `StaticCache` generation or generating without cache.
    Pads to the right with `-1`.
    """
    if (padding_length := kv_length + kv_offset - block_sequence_ids.shape[-1]) > 0:
        block_sequence_ids = F.pad(block_sequence_ids, pad=(0, padding_length), value=-1)
    return block_sequence_ids


def fast_all(tensor: torch.BoolTensor) -> torch.BoolTensor:
    """Similar to `tensor.all()`, but uses an implementation with `tensor.sum()`, which is actually much faster."""
    return tensor.sum() == tensor.numel()

        if (padding_length := kv_length + kv_offset - attention_mask.shape[-1]) > 0:

    """Similar to `tensor.all()`, but uses an implementation with `tensor.sum()`, which is actually much faster."""
    return tensor.sum() == tensor.numel()

    the element should take part in the attention computation, and False that it should not.

        q_length (`int`):

        kv_length (`int`):
            The size that the key and value states will have during the attention computation.
        kv_offset (`int`, optional):
            An optional offset to indicate at which first position the key and values states will refer to.
        q_offset (`int`, optional):
            An optional offset to indicate at which first position the query states will refer to.
        mask_function (`Callable`):
            The mask factory function describing the mask pattern.
        attention_mask (`torch.Tensor`, optional):
            The 2D attention mask corresponding to padded tokens of shape (batch_size, number_of_seen_tokens+q_length)
        local_size (`int`, optional):
            The size of the local attention, if we do not use full attention. This is used only if `allow_is_causal_skip=True`

            `torch.sdpa` instead. Default to `True`.

            Whether to allow to return `None` for the mask under conditions where we do not have to add any bias,
            i.e. full attention without any padding. Default to `False`.
        allow_torch_fix (`bool`, optional):
            Deprecated and has no effect. Will be removed in version 5.18.0.
        use_vmap (`bool`, optional):
            Whether to use `vmap` during the mask construction or not. Allows powerful custom patterns that may not be
            index-based (for the cost of speed performance). By default `False`.
        device (`torch.device` or `str`, optional):

    ## Creating a simple causal mask:

    To create the following causal mask:

        1 ■ ■ ⬚ ⬚ ⬚
        2 ■ ■ ■ ⬚ ⬚
        3 ■ ■ ■ ■ ⬚
        4 ■ ■ ■ ■ ■

    >>> tensor([[[[ True, False, False, False, False],
                  [ True,  True, False, False, False],
                  [ True,  True,  True, False, False],
                  [ True,  True,  True,  True, False],
                  [ True,  True,  True,  True,  True]]]])
    ```

        4 ⬚ ⬚ ⬚ ■ ■

    ```python

    >>> tensor([[[[ True, False, False, False, False],
                [ True,  True, False, False, False],
                [ True,  True,  True, False, False],
                [False, False, False,  True, False],
                [False, False, False,  True,  True]]]])
    ```

    else:

def _preprocess_mask_arguments(
    config: PreTrainedConfig,
    inputs_embeds: torch.Tensor,
    attention_mask: torch.Tensor | BlockMask | None,
    past_key_values: Cache | None,
    position_ids: torch.Tensor | None,
    layer_idx: int | None,
    encoder_hidden_states: torch.Tensor | None = None,
) -> tuple[bool, torch.Tensor | BlockMask | None, int, int]:
    """
    Perform some common pre-processing of the mask arguments we get from the modeling code. Mostly determine the
    key-value length and offsets, and if we should early exit or not.

    Args:
        config (`PreTrainedConfig`):
            The model config.
        inputs_embeds (`torch.Tensor`):
            The input embeddings of shape (batch_size, query_length, hidden_dim). This is used only to infer the
            batch size, query length and dtype.
        attention_mask (`torch.Tensor`, optional):
            The 2D attention mask corresponding to padded tokens of shape (batch_size, number_of_seen_tokens+q_length).
            It can also be an already prepared 4D mask, in which case it is returned as-is.
        past_key_values (`Cache`, optional):
            The past key values, if we use a cache.
        position_ids (`torch.Tensor`, optional)
            A 2D tensor of shape (batch_size, query_length) indicating the positions of each token in the sequences.
        layer_idx (`int`, optional):
            If `past_key_values` is not None, this is the layer index of the cache from which to get the key-value
            length and offset. Indeed, for hybrid caches, different layers may return different lengths.
        encoder_hidden_states (`torch.Tensor`, optional):
            The input embeddings of shape (batch_size, kv_length, hidden_dim). If provided, it is used instead of
            `inputs_embeds` to infer the kv length.

    Returns:
        early_exit (`bool`):
            Whether we should early exit mask creation, and return the mask as-is.
        attention_mask (`torch.Tensor` or `BlockMask` or `None`):
            The attention mask to either return immediately, or to use in downstream mask creation.
        packed_sequence_mask (`torch.Tensor`, optional):
            In case we detected packed sequence format, this is a tensor where each similar integer indicates that
            the tokens belong to the same sequence.
        q_length (`int`):
            The size that the query states will have during the attention computation.
        kv_length (`int`):
            The size that the key and value states will have during the attention computation.
        q_offset (`int`, optional):
            An optional offset to indicate at which first position the query states will refer to.
        kv_offset (`int`):
            An offset to indicate at which first position the key and values states will refer to.
    """
    # If the mask is already 4D, simply return as-is (it was already prepared, or it is custom)
    if isinstance(attention_mask, (torch.Tensor, BlockMask)) and len(attention_mask.shape) == 4:
        return True, attention_mask, None, None, None, None, None

    # For TGI/vLLM backends, or other custom attention without equivalent mask creation: we don't need a mask!
    # Note: it's not ideal to check the `_global_mapping` attribute instead of the object itself, however otherwise
    # full graph dynamo tracing (i.e. torch.export or compile with `fullgraph=True`) will fail on Python<3.11
    # with `torch._dynamo.exc.Unsupported: 'inline in skipfiles:Mapping.__contains__ | __contains__, skipped
    # according trace_rules.lookup SKIP_DIRS'` -- can be removed when we require Python>=3.11
    if config._attn_implementation not in ALL_MASK_ATTENTION_FUNCTIONS._global_mapping:

    if attention_mask is not None and attention_mask.ndim == 2:

    if past_key_values is not None:

        # we need the correct device

        kv_length, kv_offset = past_key_values.get_mask_sizes(q_length, layer_idx)

    else:

def create_bidirectional_mask(
    config: PreTrainedConfig,
    inputs_embeds: torch.Tensor,
    attention_mask: torch.Tensor | None,
    encoder_hidden_states: torch.Tensor | None = None,
    past_key_values: Cache | None = None,
    or_mask_function: Callable | None = None,
    and_mask_function: Callable | None = None,
    allow_is_bidirectional_skip: bool = True,
    **kwargs,
) -> torch.Tensor | BlockMask | None:
    """
    Create a standard bidirectional mask based on the attention implementation used (stored in the config).

    Args:
        config (`PreTrainedConfig`):
            The model config.
        inputs_embeds (`torch.Tensor`):
            The input embeddings of shape (batch_size, query_length, hidden_dim). This is only used to infer metadata
            such as the batch size, query length, dtype, and device.
        attention_mask (`torch.Tensor`, optional):
            The 2D attention mask corresponding to padded tokens of shape (batch_size, kv_length).
            It can also be an already prepared 4D mask of shape (batch_size, 1, query_length, kv_length),
            in which case it is returned as-is.
        encoder_hidden_states (`torch.Tensor`, optional):
            The input embeddings of shape (batch_size, kv_length, hidden_dim). If provided, it is used instead of
            `inputs_embeds` to infer the batch size, kv length and dtype.
        past_key_values (`Cache`, optional):
            The past key values, if we use a cache.
        or_mask_function (`Callable`, optional):
            An optional mask function to combine with the base mask function (by doing the union of both). This is
            useful to easily overlay another mask on top, for example for image tokens handling.
        and_mask_function (`Callable`, optional):
            An optional mask function to combine with the base mask function (by doing the intersection of both). This is
            useful to easily overlay another mask on top, for example for image tokens handling.
        allow_is_bidirectional_skip (`bool`, optional):
            Whether to allow returning `None` (no bias) when the mask is plain bidirectional with no padding. Set to
            `False` to always materialize the mask, e.g. when it is later concatenated with another mask. Defaults to
            `True`.
    """
    # If we have a hybrid cache structure, here we want to create the mask for the full layers
    if hasattr(past_key_values, "is_sliding") and False in past_key_values.is_sliding:
        layer_idx = past_key_values.is_sliding.index(False)
    else:
        layer_idx = 0

    # We ignore a few irrelevant arguments at the end as we do not have a (growing) cache here
    early_exit, attention_mask, _, q_length, kv_length, q_offset, kv_offset = _preprocess_mask_arguments(
        config, inputs_embeds, attention_mask, past_key_values, None, layer_idx, encoder_hidden_states
    )
    if early_exit:
        return attention_mask

    embeds = encoder_hidden_states if encoder_hidden_states is not None else inputs_embeds
    batch_size, dtype = embeds.shape[0], embeds.dtype
    # Use `inputs_embeds.device` to stay consistent with `_preprocess_mask_arguments`, which moves the 2D
    # `attention_mask` to that device. In model parallel setups, `encoder_hidden_states` may live on a different
    # device than `inputs_embeds` (e.g. cross-attention from a decoder to encoder states).
    device = inputs_embeds.device
    mask_factory_function = bidirectional_mask_function
    mask_interface = ALL_MASK_ATTENTION_FUNCTIONS[config._attn_implementation]

    # Defaulting to using non-vmap based mask creations except when detecting
    # users passing custom mask functions (as we cannot guarantee that they
    # are properly index-based as required by our implementation).
    use_vmap = False

    # Allow slight deviations from the base mask
    # Note that it is very important to apply this before any other deviations of the mask (such as packed sequence mask,
    # padding mask, etc) as the resulting mask may otherwise not be correct!
    if or_mask_function is not None:
        mask_factory_function = or_masks(mask_factory_function, or_mask_function)
        allow_is_bidirectional_skip = False
        use_vmap = True
    if and_mask_function is not None:
        mask_factory_function = and_masks(mask_factory_function, and_mask_function)
        allow_is_bidirectional_skip = False
        use_vmap = True

    # We now create the mask
    attention_mask = mask_interface(
        batch_size=batch_size,
        q_length=q_length,
        kv_length=kv_length,
        q_offset=q_offset,
        kv_offset=kv_offset,
        mask_function=mask_factory_function,
        attention_mask=attention_mask,
        # Additional kwargs for sdpa
        allow_is_causal_skip=False,
        allow_is_bidirectional_skip=allow_is_bidirectional_skip,
        dtype=dtype,  # Additional kwarg for eager
        config=config,  # Pass the config as well, in case someone wants to easily have their own mask_interface
        use_vmap=use_vmap,  # Short-circuit to non-vmap expansions for the mask
        device=device,
    )
    return attention_mask

    config: PreTrainedConfig,
    inputs_embeds: torch.Tensor,
    attention_mask: torch.Tensor | None,

    Create a sliding window causal mask based on the attention implementation used (stored in the config). This type
    of attention pattern was mostly democratized by Mistral. If `past_key_values` has a hybrid cache structure, this

        or_mask_function (`Callable`, optional):

            useful to easily overlay another mask on top of the sliding causal one, for example for image tokens handling.

            An optional mask function to combine with the sliding causal mask function (by doing the intersection of both). This is
            useful to easily overlay another mask on top of the sliding causal one, for example for image tokens handling.

            A tensor of same shape as input IDs indicating to which block or group each token belongs to. Tokens from

            another mask. Defaults to `True`.
    """
    # Power feature: if `is_causal` is False, then fallback to bi-directional mask for bi-directional attention
    # It allows to use decoder-only models with bi-directional attention as well
    if not getattr(config, "is_causal", True):
        return create_bidirectional_sliding_window_mask(
            config,
            inputs_embeds,
            attention_mask,
            past_key_values=past_key_values,
            or_mask_function=or_mask_function,
            and_mask_function=and_mask_function,
            allow_is_bidirectional_skip=allow_is_causal_skip,
        )

    if layer_idx is None:

            layer_idx = past_key_values.is_sliding.index(True)
        else:
            layer_idx = 0

    early_exit, attention_mask, packed_sequence_mask, q_length, kv_length, q_offset, kv_offset = (
        _preprocess_mask_arguments(config, inputs_embeds, attention_mask, past_key_values, position_ids, layer_idx)
    )
    if early_exit:
        return attention_mask

    sliding_window = getattr(config, "sliding_window", None)
    if sliding_window is None:
        raise ValueError("Could not find a `sliding_window` argument in the config, or it is not set")

    batch_size, dtype, device = inputs_embeds.shape[0], inputs_embeds.dtype, inputs_embeds.device
    mask_factory_function = sliding_window_causal_mask_function(sliding_window)
    mask_interface = ALL_MASK_ATTENTION_FUNCTIONS[config._attn_implementation]

    # Defaulting to using non-vmap based mask creations except when detecting
    # users passing custom mask functions (as we cannot guarantee that they
    # are properly index-based as required by our implementation).

    # prefill is not compiled)

        getattr(past_key_values, "is_compileable", False) and q_length == 1
    )

    # Allow slight deviations from causal mask
    # Note that it is very important to apply this before any other deviations of the mask (such as packed sequence mask,
    # padding mask, etc) as the resulting mask may otherwise not be correct!
    if or_mask_function is not None:
        mask_factory_function = or_masks(mask_factory_function, or_mask_function)
        allow_is_causal_skip = False
        use_vmap = True
    if and_mask_function is not None:
        mask_factory_function = and_masks(mask_factory_function, and_mask_function)
        allow_is_causal_skip = False
        use_vmap = True

    if packed_sequence_mask is not None:
        mask_factory_function = and_masks(mask_factory_function, packed_sequence_mask_function(packed_sequence_mask))

        allow_is_causal_skip = False

    # We now create the mask
    causal_mask = mask_interface(
        batch_size=batch_size,
        q_length=q_length,
        kv_length=kv_length,
        q_offset=q_offset,
        kv_offset=kv_offset,
        mask_function=mask_factory_function,
        attention_mask=attention_mask,
        allow_is_causal_skip=allow_is_causal_skip,  # additional kwarg for sdpa
        local_size=sliding_window,  # Additional kwarg for sdpa
        dtype=dtype,  # Additional kwarg for eager
        config=config,  # Pass the config as well, in case someone wants to easily have their own mask_interface
        use_vmap=use_vmap,  # Short-circuit to non-vmap expansions for the mask
        device=device,
    )
    return causal_mask

import zipfile, pickletools, io

for repo, rev in [("jhu-clsp/ettin-encoder-17m","987607455c61e7a5bbc85f7758e0512ea6d0ae4c"),("jhu-clsp/ettin-decoder-17m","728fb5b6b3dc5916aa20829c027143ae8eca4eeb")]:

    names = z.namelist()
    print(len(names), names[:6], names[-4:])
    pkl = [n for n in names if n.endswith("data.pkl")][0]
    data = z.read(pkl)
    globs = set()
    for op, arg, pos in pickletools.genops(data):
        if op.name in ("GLOBAL", "STACK_GLOBAL"):
            globs.add((op.name, arg))
    print(globs)
    # find STACK_GLOBAL args by tracking previous SHORT_BINUNICODE
    ops = list(pickletools.genops(data))
    sg = set()
    for i, (op, arg, pos) in enumerate(ops):
        if op.name == "STACK_GLOBAL":
            sg.add((ops[i-2][1], ops[i-1][1]))
    print(sg)
    bo = [n for n in names if n.endswith("byteorder")]
    print("byteorder", bo and z.read(bo[0]))
EOF

mx.metal.device_info is deprecated and will be removed in a future version. Use mx.device_info instead.
scaled_dot_product_attention(q: array, k: array, v: array, *, scale: float,  mask: None | str | array = None, sinks: array | None = None, force_fused: bool = False, stream: StreamOrDevice = None) -> array

        A fast implementation of multi-head attention: ``O = softmax(Q @ K.T, dim=-1) @ V``.

        Supports:

        * `Multi-Head Attention <https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762>`_
        * `Grouped Query Attention <https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13245>`_
        * `Multi-Query Attention <https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.02150>`_

        .. note::

          * The softmax operation is performed in ``float32`` regardless of
            the input precision.
          * For Grouped Query Attention and Multi-Query Attention, the ``k``
            and ``v`` inputs should not be pre-tiled to match ``q``.

        In the following the dimensions are given by:

        * ``B``: The batch size.
        * ``N_q``: The number of query heads.
        * ``N_kv``: The number of key and value heads.
        * ``T_q``: The number of queries per example.
        * ``T_kv``: The number of keys and values per example.
        * ``D``: The per-head dimension.

        Args:
            q (array): Queries with shape ``[B, N_q, T_q, D]``.
            k (array): Keys with shape ``[B, N_kv, T_kv, D]``.
            v (array): Values with shape ``[B, N_kv, T_kv, D]``.
            scale (float): Scale for queries (typically ``1.0 / sqrt(q.shape(-1)``).
            mask (str or array, optional): The mask to apply to the
               query-key scores. The mask can be an array or a string indicating
               the mask type. The only supported string type is ``"causal"``. If
               the mask is an array it can be a boolean or additive mask. The mask
               can have at most 4 dimensions and must be broadcast-compatible with
               the shape ``[B, N, T_q, T_kv]``. If an additive mask is given its
               type must promote to the promoted type of ``q``, ``k``, and ``v``.
               The ``"causal"`` mask uses lower-right alignment where the
               last query aligns with the last key.
            sinks (array, optional): An optional array of attention sinks.
               Default: ``None``.
            force_fused (bool, optional): If ``True``, use a fused kernel
               regardless of the builtin heuristics and raise error when no
               fused kernel is available. For certain configurations this would
               result in slower kernel getting used but can reduce memory
               consumption. Default: ``False``.

        Returns:
            array: The output array.

        Example:

          .. code-block:: python

            B = 2
            N_q = N_kv = 32
            T_q = T_kv = 1000
            D = 128

            q = mx.random.normal(shape=(B, N_q, T_q, D))
            k = mx.random.normal(shape=(B, N_kv, T_kv, D))
            v = mx.random.normal(shape=(B, N_kv, T_kv, D))
            scale = D ** -0.5
            out = mx.fast.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, k, v, scale=scale, mask="causal")
      
rope(a: array, dims: int, *, traditional: bool, base: float | None, scale: float, offset: int | array, freqs: array | None = None, stream: StreamOrDevice = None) -> array

        Apply rotary positional encoding to the input.

        The input is expected to be at least 3D with shape ``(B, *, T, D)`` where:
          * ``B`` is the batch size.
          * ``T`` is the sequence length.
          * ``D`` is the feature dimension.

        Args:
            a (array): The input array.
            dims (int): The feature dimensions to be rotated. If the input feature
              is larger than dims then the rest is left unchanged.
            traditional (bool): If set to ``True`` choose the traditional
              implementation which rotates consecutive dimensions.
            base (float, optional): The base used to compute angular frequency for
              each dimension in the positional encodings. Exactly one of ``base`` and
              ``freqs`` must be ``None``.
            scale (float): The scale used to scale the positions.
            offset (int or array): The position offset to start at. If an
              :obj:`array` is given it can be a scalar or vector of ``B``
              offsets for each example in the batch.
            freqs (array, optional): Optional frequencies to use with RoPE.
              If set, the ``base`` parameter must be ``None``. Default: ``None``.

        Returns:
            array: The output array.
      
layer_norm(x: array, weight: array | None, bias: array | None, eps: float, *, stream: StreamOrDevice = None) -> array

        Layer normalization.

        The normalization is with respect to the last axis of the input ``x``.

        Args:
            x (array): Input array.
            weight (array, optional): A multiplicative weight to scale the result by.
              The ``weight`` should be one-dimensional with the same size
              as the last axis of ``x``. If set to ``None`` then no scaling happens.
            bias (array, optional): An additive offset to be added to the result.
              The ``bias`` should be one-dimensional with the same size
              as the last axis of ``x``. If set to ``None`` then no translation happens.
            eps (float): A small additive constant for numerical stability.

        Returns:
            array: The output array.

"""Model configuration parsed from a Hugging Face ``config.json``.

Both config generations are accepted:

* old (what the Ettin checkpoints ship): ``global_attn_every_n_layers``,
  ``global_rope_theta``, ``local_rope_theta``;
* new (transformers >= 5): ``layer_types`` and ``rope_parameters`` keyed by layer type.

Defaults mirror ``ModernBertConfig`` / ``ModernBertDecoderConfig`` in transformers 5.x.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

ENCODER_MODEL_TYPE = "modernbert"
DECODER_MODEL_TYPE = "modernbert-decoder"
FULL = "full_attention"
SLIDING = "sliding_attention"

# transformers' ModernBert*Config.default_theta
_DEFAULT_THETA = {FULL: 160_000.0, SLIDING: 10_000.0}


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class EttinConfig:
    model_type: str
    vocab_size: int
    hidden_size: int
    intermediate_size: int
    num_hidden_layers: int
    num_attention_heads: int
    layer_types: tuple[str, ...]
    rope_theta: dict[str, float]
    local_attention: int
    hidden_activation: str = "gelu"
    classifier_activation: str = "gelu"
    norm_eps: float = 1e-5
    norm_bias: bool = False
    attention_bias: bool = False
    mlp_bias: bool = False
    classifier_bias: bool = False
    decoder_bias: bool = True
    tie_word_embeddings: bool = True
    max_position_embeddings: int = 8192
    pad_token_id: int | None = 50283
    bos_token_id: int | None = 50281
    eos_token_id: int | list[int] | None = 50282
    cls_token_id: int | None = 50281
    sep_token_id: int | None = 50282
    raw: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict, repr=False, compare=False)

    @property
    def is_decoder(self) -> bool:
        return self.model_type == DECODER_MODEL_TYPE

    @property
    def head_dim(self) -> int:
        return self.hidden_size // self.num_attention_heads

    @property
    def sliding_window(self) -> int:
        """Half of ``local_attention`` (64 for 128), exactly as HF defines it.

        Encoder sliding layers attend to keys with ``|q - k| <= sliding_window``;
        decoder sliding layers to keys with ``q - sliding_window < k <= q``.
        """
        return self.local_attention // 2

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, d: dict[str, Any]) -> EttinConfig:
        model_type = d.get("model_type")
        if model_type not in (ENCODER_MODEL_TYPE, DECODER_MODEL_TYPE):
            raise ValueError(f"unsupported model_type {model_type!r}")
        if model_type == DECODER_MODEL_TYPE and not d.get("is_causal", True):
            # HF would silently switch the decoder to bidirectional masks; a KV cache
            # makes no sense then, so refuse instead of guessing.
            raise NotImplementedError("modernbert-decoder with is_causal=False is not supported")

        hidden = d.get("hidden_size", 768)
        heads = d.get("num_attention_heads", 12)
        if hidden % heads:
            raise ValueError(f"hidden_size {hidden} is not a multiple of num_attention_heads {heads}")
        n_layers = d.get("num_hidden_layers", 22)

        layer_types = d.get("layer_types")
        if layer_types is None:
            every = d.get("global_attn_every_n_layers", 3)
            layer_types = [SLIDING if i % every else FULL for i in range(n_layers)]
        layer_types = tuple(layer_types)
        if len(layer_types) != n_layers or not set(layer_types) <= {FULL, SLIDING}:
            raise ValueError(f"bad layer_types {layer_types!r} for {n_layers} layers")

        local_attention = d.get("local_attention", 128)
        if SLIDING in layer_types and not local_attention:
            raise ValueError("sliding_attention layers need a positive local_attention")

        return cls(
            model_type=model_type,
            vocab_size=d.get("vocab_size", 50368),
            hidden_size=hidden,
            intermediate_size=int(d.get("intermediate_size", 1152)),
            num_hidden_layers=n_layers,
            num_attention_heads=heads,
            layer_types=layer_types,
            rope_theta=_parse_rope_theta(d),
            local_attention=local_attention or 0,
            hidden_activation=d.get("hidden_activation", "gelu"),
            classifier_activation=d.get("classifier_activation", "gelu"),
            norm_eps=d.get("norm_eps", 1e-5),
            norm_bias=d.get("norm_bias", False),
            attention_bias=d.get("attention_bias", False),
            mlp_bias=d.get("mlp_bias", False),
            classifier_bias=d.get("classifier_bias", False),
            decoder_bias=d.get("decoder_bias", True),
            tie_word_embeddings=d.get("tie_word_embeddings", True),
            max_position_embeddings=d.get("max_position_embeddings", 8192),
            pad_token_id=d.get("pad_token_id", 50283),
            bos_token_id=d.get("bos_token_id", 50281),
            eos_token_id=d.get("eos_token_id", 50282),
            cls_token_id=d.get("cls_token_id", 50281),
            sep_token_id=d.get("sep_token_id", 50282),
            raw=dict(d),
        )

"""Attention masks and attention kernels.

Mask semantics follow ``transformers.masking_utils`` (eager/sdpa paths):

* encoder full layers:    every key, minus padded keys;
* encoder sliding layers: ``|q - k| <= w`` (``sliding_window_bidirectional_overlay``);
* decoder full layers:    ``k <= q``;
* decoder sliding layers: ``q - w < k <= q`` (``sliding_window_overlay`` + causal).

``w`` is ``config.sliding_window`` (= ``local_attention // 2``). A 2D ``attention_mask``
(1 = token, 0 = padding) indexed by absolute position removes padded keys. Rows of
padded *queries* ignore the padding mask instead of being fully masked, so they stay
finite (HF fills them with a uniform softmax over ``finfo.min``); their values are
never read by real tokens.

Every mask is built once per forward call per layer type and closed over by an
``attend(q, k, v, scale) -> (B, Lq, H*D)`` callable that each layer calls.

            return None
        if need_causal and not need_window and kv_last == q_last:
            return "causal"

    qi = mx.arange(q_start, q_start + q_len)[:, None]
    ki = mx.arange(kv_start, kv_start + kv_len)[None, :]
    mask = None

        mask = in_window if mask is None else mask & in_window

        valid = attention_mask.astype(mx.bool_)
        key_ok = valid[:, None, None, kv_start : kv_start + kv_len]
        query_pad = ~valid[:, None, q_start : q_start + q_len, None]

        mask = mx.broadcast_to(mask[:, None], (batch, num_heads, n_blocks, block, span))

"""KV caches for the decoder.

``KVCache`` (full-attention layers) keeps every key in a buffer that grows in steps,
written in place. ``SlidingKVCache`` mirrors HF's ``DynamicSlidingWindowLayer``: it
stores the last ``window - 1`` keys and returns them concatenated with the new ones,
which is exactly the set a decoder sliding layer (``q - window < k <= q``) can see
for a single new token. Keys are cached after RoPE.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import mlx.core as mx


class KVCache:
    step = 256

    def __init__(self):
        self.keys: mx.array | None = None
        self.values: mx.array | None = None
        self.offset = 0

    def kv_start(self) -> int:
        """Absolute position of the first key that ``update_and_fetch`` will return."""
        return 0

    def update_and_fetch(self, keys: mx.array, values: mx.array) -> tuple[mx.array, mx.array]:
        prev, n = self.offset, keys.shape[2]
        if self.keys is None or prev + n > self.keys.shape[2]:
            B, H, _, D = keys.shape
            capacity = ((prev + n + self.step - 1) // self.step) * self.step
            new_k = mx.zeros((B, H, capacity, D), keys.dtype)
            new_v = mx.zeros((B, H, capacity, D), values.dtype)
            if self.keys is not None:
                new_k[..., :prev, :] = self.keys[..., :prev, :]
                new_v[..., :prev, :] = self.values[..., :prev, :]
            self.keys, self.values = new_k, new_v
        self.keys[..., prev : prev + n, :] = keys
        self.values[..., prev : prev + n, :] = values
        self.offset += n
        return self.keys[..., : self.offset, :], self.values[..., : self.offset, :]


class SlidingKVCache:
    def __init__(self, window: int):
        self.keep = window - 1
        self.keys: mx.array | None = None
        self.values: mx.array | None = None
        self.offset = 0

    def kv_start(self) -> int:
        return self.offset - (0 if self.keys is None else self.keys.shape[2])

    def update_and_fetch(self, keys: mx.array, values: mx.array) -> tuple[mx.array, mx.array]:
        if self.keys is not None:
            keys = mx.concatenate([self.keys, keys], axis=2)
            values = mx.concatenate([self.values, values], axis=2)
        self.offset += keys.shape[2] - (0 if self.keys is None else self.keys.shape[2])
        start = max(keys.shape[2] - self.keep, 0)
        self.keys, self.values = keys[:, :, start:], values[:, :, start:]
        return keys, values

"""Attention masks and attention kernels.

Mask semantics follow ``transformers.masking_utils`` (eager/sdpa paths):

* encoder full layers:    every key, minus padded keys;
* encoder sliding layers: ``|q - k| <= w`` (``sliding_window_bidirectional_overlay``);
* decoder full layers:    ``k <= q``;
* decoder sliding layers: ``q - w < k <= q`` (``sliding_window_overlay`` + causal).

``w`` is ``config.sliding_window`` (= ``local_attention // 2``). A 2D ``attention_mask``
(1 = token, 0 = padding) indexed by absolute position removes padded keys. Rows of
padded *queries* ignore the padding mask instead of being fully masked, so they stay
finite (HF fills them with a uniform softmax over ``finfo.min``); their values are
never read by real tokens.

Every mask is built once per forward call per layer type and closed over by an
``attend(q, k, v, scale) -> (B, Lq, H*D)`` callable that each layer calls.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from collections.abc import Callable

import mlx.core as mx

Attend = Callable[[mx.array, mx.array, mx.array, float], mx.array]
Mask = mx.array | str | None


def build_mask(
    q_start: int,
    q_len: int,
    kv_start: int,
    kv_len: int,
    *,
    causal: bool,
    window: int | None,
    attention_mask: mx.array | None = None,
) -> Mask:
    """Boolean mask (True = attend) broadcastable to ``(B, H, q_len, kv_len)``.

    Queries sit at absolute positions ``[q_start, q_start + q_len)`` and keys at
    ``[kv_start, kv_start + kv_len)``. Returns ``None`` when nothing is masked and
    ``"causal"`` when the plain lower-right causal mask is exact.
    """
    q_last, kv_last = q_start + q_len - 1, kv_start + kv_len - 1
    if causal:
        need_causal = kv_last > q_start
        need_window = window is not None and kv_start <= q_last - window
    else:
        need_causal = False
        need_window = window is not None and max(q_last - kv_start, kv_last - q_start) > window

    if attention_mask is None:
        if not (need_causal or need_window):
            return None
        if need_causal and not need_window and kv_last == q_last:
            return "causal"

    qi = mx.arange(q_start, q_start + q_len)[:, None]
    ki = mx.arange(kv_start, kv_start + kv_len)[None, :]
    mask = None
    if need_causal:
        mask = ki <= qi
    if need_window:
        in_window = (ki > qi - window) if causal else (mx.abs(qi - ki) <= window)
        mask = in_window if mask is None else mask & in_window
    if attention_mask is not None:
        valid = attention_mask.astype(mx.bool_)
        key_ok = valid[:, None, None, kv_start : kv_start + kv_len]
        if mask is None:
            # Unrestricted attention: every query row sees all real keys, so a
            # (B, 1, 1, kv_len) key mask is enough (rows with no real key at all
            # are let through instead of producing NaN).
            return key_ok | ~mx.any(key_ok, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
        query_pad = ~valid[:, None, q_start : q_start + q_len, None]
        mask = mask & (key_ok | query_pad)
    return mask


def dense_attention(mask: Mask) -> Attend:
    def attend(q, k, v, scale):
        B, _, L, _ = q.shape
        out = mx.fast.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, k, v, scale=scale, mask=mask)
        return out.transpose(0, 2, 1, 3).reshape(B, L, -1)

    return attend


def blocked_local_attention(
    batch: int,
    length: int,
    num_heads: int,
    *,
    window: int,
    causal: bool,
    block: int,
    attention_mask: mx.array | None = None,
) -> Attend:
    """Sliding-window attention over a full sequence in O(L * window).

    Queries are split into blocks of ``block`` rows. Block ``i`` attends to the
    contiguous key span that any of its rows can see: ``[i*block - w, (i+1)*block + w)``
    for the bidirectional window and ``[i*block - w + 1, (i+1)*block)`` for the causal
    one. The spans overlap, so they are exposed as an ``as_strided`` view of the padded
    keys (no copy) and fed to the fused SDPA kernel as a ``(B*H, n_blocks, span, D)``
    batch. The exact window/padding mask is applied inside each span, so the result
    equals dense masked attention up to float summation order.
    """
    n_blocks = math.ceil(length / block)
    padded = n_blocks * block
    left = window if not causal else window - 1
    right = (padded - length) + (0 if causal else window)
    span = block + left + (0 if causal else window)
    total = left + padded + right

    # Absolute key position for (block i, slot j) and query position for (block i, row r).
    k_pos = mx.arange(n_blocks)[:, None] * block - left + mx.arange(span)[None, :]
    q_pos = mx.arange(n_blocks)[:, None] * block + mx.arange(block)[None, :]
    rel = k_pos[:, None, :] - q_pos[:, :, None]  # (n_blocks, block, span)
    mask = (rel <= 0) & (rel > -window) if causal else mx.abs(rel) <= window
    key_ok = (k_pos >= 0) & (k_pos < length)  # (n_blocks, span)
    if attention_mask is None:
        mask = (mask & key_ok[:, None, :])[None]  # (1, n_blocks, block, span)
    else:
        valid = attention_mask.astype(mx.bool_)
        k_valid = mx.take(valid, mx.clip(k_pos, 0, length - 1).reshape(-1), axis=1)
        k_valid = k_valid.reshape(batch, n_blocks, 1, span) & key_ok[None, :, None, :]
        q_valid = mx.pad(valid, [(0, 0), (0, padded - length)]).reshape(batch, n_blocks, block, 1)
        mask = mask[None] & (k_valid | ~q_valid)  # (B, n_blocks, block, span)
        mask = mx.broadcast_to(mask[:, None], (batch, num_heads, n_blocks, block, span))
        mask = mask.reshape(batch * num_heads, n_blocks, block, span)

    def windows(x):
        B, H, _, D = x.shape
        x = mx.pad(x, [(0, 0), (0, 0), (left, right), (0, 0)])
        return mx.as_strided(x, (B * H, n_blocks, span, D), (total * D, block * D, D, 1))

    def attend(q, k, v, scale):
        B, H, L, D = q.shape
        qb = mx.pad(q, [(0, 0), (0, 0), (0, padded - L), (0, 0)]).reshape(B * H, n_blocks, block, D)
        out = mx.fast.scaled_dot_product_attention(qb, windows(k), windows(v), scale=scale, mask=mask)
        out = out.reshape(B, H, padded, D)[:, :, :L]
        return out.transpose(0, 2, 1, 3).reshape(B, L, -1)

    return attend

"""Prefill/decode loop for the decoder: greedy, temperature and top-p sampling."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Iterator

import mlx.core as mx

from .decoder import EttinDecoder


def top_p_filter(logits: mx.array, top_p: float) -> mx.array:
    """HF ``TopPLogitsWarper``: drop the least likely tokens whose cumulative probability
    is ``<= 1 - top_p``; the most likely token is always kept."""
    order = mx.argsort(logits, axis=-1)  # ascending
    sorted_logits = mx.take_along_axis(logits, order, axis=-1)
    cumulative = mx.cumsum(mx.softmax(sorted_logits, axis=-1), axis=-1)
    remove_sorted = cumulative <= (1.0 - top_p)
    remove_sorted[..., -1] = False
    remove = mx.put_along_axis(mx.zeros_like(remove_sorted), order, remove_sorted, axis=-1)
    return mx.where(remove, -mx.inf, logits)


def sample(logits: mx.array, temperature: float = 0.0, top_p: float = 1.0, key: mx.array | None = None) -> mx.array:
    """``(B, V)`` logits -> ``(B,)`` token ids. ``temperature == 0`` is greedy."""
    if temperature == 0:
        return mx.argmax(logits, axis=-1)
    logits = logits.astype(mx.float32) / temperature
    if top_p < 1.0:
        logits = top_p_filter(logits, top_p)
    return mx.random.categorical(logits, key=key)


def generate_step(
    model: EttinDecoder,
    input_ids: mx.array,
    max_new_tokens: int,
    *,
    attention_mask: mx.array | None = None,
    temperature: float = 0.0,
    top_p: float = 1.0,
    seed: int | None = None,
) -> Iterator[mx.array]:
    """Yield ``(B,)`` token arrays: one prefill pass over the prompt, then one token per step.

    The next step is scheduled with ``mx.async_eval`` before the current token is
    yielded, so graph construction overlaps with GPU work.
    """
    cache = model.make_cache()
    key = mx.random.key(seed) if seed is not None else None
    batch = input_ids.shape[0]

    def step(ids):
        nonlocal key, attention_mask
        logits = model(ids, attention_mask=attention_mask, cache=cache, logits_to_keep=1)[:, -1]
        sub = None
        if key is not None:
            key, sub = mx.random.split(key)
        return sample(logits, temperature, top_p, sub)

    token = step(input_ids)
    mx.async_eval(token)
    for n in range(max_new_tokens):
        if n + 1 < max_new_tokens:
            if attention_mask is not None:
                attention_mask = mx.concatenate([attention_mask, mx.ones((batch, 1), attention_mask.dtype)], axis=1)
            next_token = step(token[:, None])
            mx.async_eval(next_token)
        yield token
        if n + 1 < max_new_tokens:
            token = next_token

    """HF ``TopPLogitsWarper``: drop the least likely tokens whose cumulative probability
    is ``<= 1 - top_p``; the most likely token is always kept."""
    order = mx.argsort(logits, axis=-1)  # ascending

    cumulative = mx.cumsum(mx.softmax(sorted_logits, axis=-1), axis=-1)
    remove_sorted = cumulative <= (1.0 - top_p)
    remove_sorted[..., -1] = False
    remove = mx.put_along_axis(mx.zeros_like(remove_sorted), order, remove_sorted, axis=-1)
    return mx.where(remove, -mx.inf, logits)

"""Reference outputs from HF transformers (FP32, CPU, eager attention) -> tests/data/<model>.npz.

Usage:
    uv run python tools/make_reference.py                       # default test models
    uv run python tools/make_reference.py --models ettin-encoder-150m ettin-decoder-1b

Full logits for a 2048-token case are ~400 MB, so per case we store

* ``hidden``  - ``model.final_norm`` output (last hidden state),
* ``head``    - prediction-head output, i.e. the input of the vocab projection,
* ``top1``/``margin`` - argmax of HF's full logits and the top-1/top-2 gap,
* ``sample_logits`` at ``sample_pos`` - HF logits verbatim for a few positions.

Tests rebuild reference logits as ``head @ W.T + b`` from the checkpoint tensors; the
tool checks that this reconstruction matches HF's own logits (``meta.reconstruction``).
This file uses torch/transformers and is never imported by the runtime package.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import torch
import transformers
from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoModelForMaskedLM, AutoTokenizer

from ettin_mlx.revisions import HF_ORG, PINNED_REVISIONS

DATA_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "tests" / "data"
DEFAULT_MODELS = ["ettin-encoder-17m", "ettin-decoder-17m", "ettin-encoder-32m", "ettin-decoder-32m"]

# (name, row lengths, corpus offsets). "padded" is a right-padded batch of mixed lengths.
CASES = [
    ("short", [8], [0]),
    ("medium", [300], [100]),
    ("long", [2048], [500]),
    ("padded", [300, 129, 64, 7], [3000, 3400, 3800, 4200]),
]
GEN_PROMPTS = ["The capital of France is", "def fibonacci(n):"]
GEN_LONG_PROMPT = (4600, 150)  # corpus offset, length in tokens
GEN_NEW_TOKENS = 64
FILL_MASK_TEXT = "The capital of France is {mask}."
MASK_RATE = 0.15


def corpus_ids(tokenizer) -> list[int]:
    """Natural text: the Ettin model card at the pinned encoder-17m revision."""
    path = hf_hub_download(f"{HF_ORG}/ettin-encoder-17m", "README.md", revision=PINNED_REVISIONS["ettin-encoder-17m"])
    return tokenizer(Path(path).read_text(), add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"]


def build_case(name, lengths, offsets, corpus, tok, is_decoder, rng):
    rows = []
    for n, off in zip(lengths, offsets):
        row = [tok.cls_token_id] + corpus[off : off + n - 2] + [tok.sep_token_id]
        assert len(row) == n, (name, n, len(row))
        if not is_decoder:  # MLM-style inputs: mask ~15% of the non-special tokens
            idx = rng.choice(np.arange(1, n - 1), size=max(1, int(MASK_RATE * (n - 2))), replace=False)
            for i in idx:
                row[i] = tok.mask_token_id
        rows.append(row)
    width = max(lengths)
    ids = np.full((len(rows), width), tok.pad_token_id, dtype=np.int64)
    mask = np.zeros((len(rows), width), dtype=np.int64)
    for i, row in enumerate(rows):
        ids[i, : len(row)] = row
        mask[i, : len(row)] = 1
    return ids, mask


def sample_positions(mask: np.ndarray, rng, window: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """A few (row, pos) pairs: sequence ends, window edges, and random positions."""
    picks = set()
    for r, n in enumerate(mask.sum(1)):
        for p in [0, 1, n - 1, n - 2, window, window + 1, 2 * window, 2 * window + 1, n // 2]:
            if 0 <= p < n:
                picks.add((r, int(p)))
        for p in rng.choice(n, size=min(4, n), replace=False):
            picks.add((r, int(p)))
    return np.array(sorted(picks), dtype=np.int32)


@torch.no_grad()
def make_reference(short_name: str, out_dir: Path = DATA_DIR) -> Path:
    repo, revision = f"{HF_ORG}/{short_name}", PINNED_REVISIONS[short_name]
    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(repo, revision=revision)
    is_decoder = "decoder" in AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(repo, revision=revision).__class__.__name__.lower() or (
        json.loads(Path(hf_hub_download(repo, "config.json", revision=revision)).read_text())["model_type"]
        == "modernbert-decoder"
    )
    cls = AutoModelForCausalLM if is_decoder else AutoModelForMaskedLM
    model = cls.from_pretrained(repo, revision=revision, attn_implementation="eager", dtype=torch.float32).eval()
    head = model.lm_head if is_decoder else model.head
    weight = model.decoder.weight.double()
    bias = model.decoder.bias.double() if model.decoder.bias is not None else 0.0
    window = model.config.sliding_window

    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
    corpus = corpus_ids(tok)
    out: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}
    recon_err = 0.0
    for name, lengths, offsets in CASES:
        ids, mask = build_case(name, lengths, offsets, corpus, tok, is_decoder, rng)
        t_ids, t_mask = torch.from_numpy(ids), torch.from_numpy(mask)
        hidden = model.model(input_ids=t_ids, attention_mask=t_mask).last_hidden_state
        head_out = head(hidden)
        logits = model.decoder(head_out)
        full = model(input_ids=t_ids, attention_mask=t_mask).logits

    uv run python tools/make_reference.py                       # default test models
    uv run python tools/make_reference.py --models ettin-encoder-150m ettin-decoder-1b

Full logits for a 2048-token case are ~400 MB, so per case we store

* ``hidden``  - ``model.final_norm`` output (last hidden state),
* ``head``    - prediction-head output, i.e. the input of the vocab projection,
* ``top1``/``margin`` - argmax of HF's full logits and the top-1/top-2 gap,
* ``sample_logits`` at ``sample_pos`` - HF logits verbatim for a few positions.

Tests rebuild reference logits as ``head @ W.T + b`` from the checkpoint tensors; the
tool checks that this reconstruction matches HF's own logits (``meta.reconstruction``).
This file uses torch/transformers and is never imported by the runtime package.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import torch
import transformers
from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoModelForMaskedLM, AutoTokenizer

from ettin_mlx.revisions import HF_ORG, PINNED_REVISIONS

DATA_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "tests" / "data"
DEFAULT_MODELS = ["ettin-encoder-17m", "ettin-decoder-17m", "ettin-encoder-32m", "ettin-decoder-32m"]

# (name, row lengths, corpus offsets). "padded" is a right-padded batch of mixed lengths.
CASES = [
    ("short", [8], [0]),
    ("medium", [300], [100]),
    ("long", [2048], [500]),
    ("padded", [300, 129, 64, 7], [3000, 3400, 3800, 4200]),
]
GEN_PROMPTS = ["The capital of France is", "def fibonacci(n):"]
GEN_LONG_PROMPT = (4600, 150)  # corpus offset, length in tokens
GEN_NEW_TOKENS = 64
FILL_MASK_TEXT = "The capital of France is {mask}."
MASK_RATE = 0.15


def corpus_ids(tokenizer) -> list[int]:
    """Natural text: the Ettin model card at the pinned encoder-17m revision."""
    path = hf_hub_download(f"{HF_ORG}/ettin-encoder-17m", "README.md", revision=PINNED_REVISIONS["ettin-encoder-17m"])
    return tokenizer(Path(path).read_text(), add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"]


def build_case(name, lengths, offsets, corpus, tok, is_decoder, rng):
    rows = []
    for n, off in zip(lengths, offsets):
        row = [tok.cls_token_id] + corpus[off : off + n - 2] + [tok.sep_token_id]
        assert len(row) == n, (name, n, len(row))
        if not is_decoder:  # MLM-style inputs: mask ~15% of the non-special tokens
            idx = rng.choice(np.arange(1, n - 1), size=max(1, int(MASK_RATE * (n - 2))), replace=False)
            for i in idx:
                row[i] = tok.mask_token_id
        rows.append(row)
    width = max(lengths)
    ids = np.full((len(rows), width), tok.pad_token_id, dtype=np.int64)
    mask = np.zeros((len(rows), width), dtype=np.int64)
    for i, row in enumerate(rows):
        ids[i, : len(row)] = row
        mask[i, : len(row)] = 1
    return ids, mask


def sample_positions(mask: np.ndarray, rng, window: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """A few (row, pos) pairs: sequence ends, window edges, and random positions."""
    picks = set()
    for r, n in enumerate(mask.sum(1)):
        for p in [0, 1, n - 1, n - 2, window, window + 1, 2 * window, 2 * window + 1, n // 2]:
            if 0 <= p < n:
                picks.add((r, int(p)))
        for p in rng.choice(n, size=min(4, n), replace=False):
            picks.add((r, int(p)))
    return np.array(sorted(picks), dtype=np.int32)


@torch.no_grad()
def make_reference(short_name: str, out_dir: Path = DATA_DIR) -> Path:
    repo, revision = f"{HF_ORG}/{short_name}", PINNED_REVISIONS[short_name]
    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(repo, revision=revision)
    is_decoder = "decoder" in AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(repo, revision=revision).__class__.__name__.lower() or (
        json.loads(Path(hf_hub_download(repo, "config.json", revision=revision)).read_text())["model_type"]
        == "modernbert-decoder"
    )
    cls = AutoModelForCausalLM if is_decoder else AutoModelForMaskedLM
    model = cls.from_pretrained(repo, revision=revision, attn_implementation="eager", dtype=torch.float32).eval()
    head = model.lm_head if is_decoder else model.head
    weight = model.decoder.weight.double()
    bias = model.decoder.bias.double() if model.decoder.bias is not None else 0.0
    window = model.config.sliding_window

    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
    corpus = corpus_ids(tok)
    out: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}
    recon_err = 0.0
    for name, lengths, offsets in CASES:
        ids, mask = build_case(name, lengths, offsets, corpus, tok, is_decoder, rng)
        t_ids, t_mask = torch.from_numpy(ids), torch.from_numpy(mask)
        hidden = model.model(input_ids=t_ids, attention_mask=t_mask).last_hidden_state
        head_out = head(hidden)
        logits = model.decoder(head_out)
        full = model(input_ids=t_ids, attention_mask=t_mask).logits
        assert torch.equal(full, logits), "manual head path differs from model.forward"
        recon = head_out.double() @ weight.T + bias
        recon_err = max(recon_err, (recon - logits.double()).abs().max().item())
        top2 = logits.topk(2, dim=-1).values
        pos = sample_positions(mask, rng, window)
        out |= {
            f"{name}/input_ids": ids.astype(np.int32),
            f"{name}/attention_mask": mask.astype(np.int32),
            f"{name}/hidden": hidden.numpy(),
            f"{name}/head": head_out.numpy(),
            f"{name}/top1": logits.argmax(-1).numpy().astype(np.int32),
            f"{name}/margin": (top2[..., 0] - top2[..., 1]).numpy(),
            f"{name}/sample_pos": pos,
            f"{name}/sample_logits": logits[pos[:, 0], pos[:, 1]].numpy(),
        }

    if is_decoder:
        model.generation_config.eos_token_id = None  # always produce GEN_NEW_TOKENS tokens
        prompts = [tok(p)["input_ids"][:-1] for p in GEN_PROMPTS]  # [CLS] text, no trailing [SEP]
        off, n = GEN_LONG_PROMPT
        prompts.append([tok.cls_token_id] + corpus[off : off + n - 1])
        for i, prompt in enumerate(prompts):
            gen = model.generate(
                torch.tensor([prompt]), attention_mask=torch.ones(1, len(prompt), dtype=torch.long),
                max_new_tokens=GEN_NEW_TOKENS, do_sample=False, pad_token_id=tok.pad_token_id,
            )
            out[f"gen/{i}/prompt"] = np.array(prompt, dtype=np.int32)
            out[f"gen/{i}/tokens"] = gen[0, len(prompt) :].numpy().astype(np.int32)
    else:
        ids = tok(FILL_MASK_TEXT.format(mask=tok.mask_token), return_tensors="pt")["input_ids"]
        logits = model(input_ids=ids).logits[0, (ids[0] == tok.mask_token_id).nonzero()[0, 0]]
        out["fill_mask/input_ids"] = ids.numpy().astype(np.int32)
        out["fill_mask/top5"] = logits.topk(5).indices.numpy().astype(np.int32)

    assert recon_err < 1e-4, f"head @ W.T + b does not reproduce HF logits (max abs {recon_err})"
    meta = {
        "model": short_name, "repo": repo, "revision": revision, "is_decoder": is_decoder,
        "transformers": transformers.__version__, "torch": torch.__version__,
        "attn_implementation": model.config._attn_implementation, "dtype": "float32", "device": "cpu",
        "reconstruction_max_abs": recon_err,
    }
    out["meta"] = np.array(json.dumps(meta))
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path = out_dir / f"{short_name}.npz"
    tmp = path.with_suffix(".tmp.npz")
    np.savez(tmp, **out)
    tmp.replace(path)
    return path


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument("--models", nargs="+", default=DEFAULT_MODELS, choices=sorted(PINNED_REVISIONS))
    parser.add_argument("--out-dir", type=Path, default=DATA_DIR)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    torch.set_num_threads(max(1, torch.get_num_threads()))
    for name in args.models:
        path = make_reference(name, args.out_dir)
        meta = json.loads(str(np.load(path)["meta"]))
        print(f"{name}: wrote {path} ({path.stat().st_size / 1e6:.1f} MB), reconstruction max abs {meta['reconstruction_max_abs']:.2e}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import json
import subprocess
import sys
from collections import OrderedDict
from pathlib import Path

import mlx.core as mx
import numpy as np
import pytest

from ettin_mlx.loading import load_model, read_checkpoint, snapshot

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
DATA = ROOT / "tests" / "data"
REPORT = DATA / "parity_report.json"

DEFAULT_MODELS = ["ettin-encoder-17m", "ettin-decoder-17m", "ettin-encoder-32m", "ettin-decoder-32m"]
LARGE_MODELS = [
    f"ettin-{kind}-{size}" for size in ("68m", "150m", "400m", "1b") for kind in ("encoder", "decoder")
]


def models(kind: str | None = None):
    """Default models plus the opt-in ``large`` ones, optionally filtered by encoder/decoder."""
    params = [pytest.param(m, id=m) for m in DEFAULT_MODELS]
    params += [pytest.param(m, id=m, marks=pytest.mark.large) for m in LARGE_MODELS]
    return [p for p in params if kind is None or f"-{kind}-" in p.values[0]]


_refs: dict[str, dict] = {}


def reference(name: str) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]:
    """HF reference outputs for ``name``; generated with tools/make_reference.py if missing."""
    if name not in _refs:
        path = DATA / f"{name}.npz"
        if not path.exists():
            subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(ROOT / "tools" / "make_reference.py"), "--models", name], check=True)
        with np.load(path) as f:
            _refs.clear()
            _refs[name] = {k: f[k] for k in f.files}
    return _refs[name]


_models: OrderedDict = OrderedDict()


def model(name: str, dtype: str = "float32", **kwargs):
    """Loaded MLX model; keeps only the two most recent to bound memory with the 1B checkpoints."""
    key = (name, dtype, tuple(sorted(kwargs.items())))
    if key not in _models:
        while len(_models) >= 2:
            _models.popitem(last=False)
        mx.clear_cache()
        _models[key] = load_model(name, dtype=dtype, **kwargs)
    _models.move_to_end(key)
    return _models[key]


_vocab: dict[str, tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray | None]] = {}


def vocab_projection(name: str) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray | None]:
    """The checkpoint's own (W, b) of the vocab projection, read straight from the file."""
    if name not in _vocab:
        _vocab.clear()
        raw = read_checkpoint(snapshot(name))
        cfg = json.loads((snapshot(name) / "config.json").read_text())
        w_key = "model.embeddings.tok_embeddings.weight" if cfg.get("tie_word_embeddings", True) else "decoder.weight"
        bias = np.array(raw["decoder.bias"]) if "decoder.bias" in raw else None
        _vocab[name] = (np.array(raw[w_key]), bias)
    return _vocab[name]


def reference_logits(name: str, case: str) -> np.ndarray:
    """HF logits rebuilt as ``head @ W.T + b`` (float32; see tools/make_reference.py)."""
    w, b = vocab_projection(name)
    out = reference(name)[f"{case}/head"] @ w.T
    return out if b is None else out + b


class Report:
    """Collects measured numbers across the session into tests/data/parity_report.json."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.data = json.loads(REPORT.read_text()) if REPORT.exists() else {}

    def add(self, model_name: str, key: str, values: dict):
        self.data.setdefault(model_name, {})[key] = values

    def save(self):
        DATA.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        REPORT.write_text(json.dumps(self.data, indent=1, sort_keys=True))


@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def report():
    r = Report()
    yield r
    r.save()

"""Tests 1, 3 (HF parity at window edges), 4 and 7: logits vs HF transformers FP32 CPU eager."""

import mlx.core as mx
import numpy as np
import pytest

from helpers import CASES, compare, model, models, reference, reference_logits

ATOL = 1e-3


def run(name: str, case: str, dtype: str = "float32") -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    ref = reference(name)
    ids, mask = ref[f"{case}/input_ids"], ref[f"{case}/attention_mask"]
    m = model(name, dtype)
    # Pass the mask only for padded batches, as a user would.
    attn = mx.array(mask) if not mask.all() else None
    if m.config.is_decoder:
        hidden = m.hidden_states(mx.array(ids), attn)
    else:
        hidden = m.encode(mx.array(ids), attn)
    logits = m.logits(hidden)
    return np.array(logits.astype(mx.float32)), np.array(hidden.astype(mx.float32))


@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", models())
@pytest.mark.parametrize("case", CASES)
def test_fp32_logits_match_hf(name, case, report):
    """Tests 1 (encoders) and 4 (decoders): max abs diff < 1e-3 and 100% top-1 on every real position."""
    ref = reference(name)
    mask = ref[f"{case}/attention_mask"]
    logits, hidden = run(name, case)
    stats = compare(logits, reference_logits(name, case), ref[f"{case}/top1"], mask)

    pos = ref[f"{case}/sample_pos"]
    stats["sampled_hf_logits_max_abs"] = float(np.abs(logits[pos[:, 0], pos[:, 1]] - ref[f"{case}/sample_logits"]).max())
    valid = mask.astype(bool)
    stats["hidden_max_abs"] = float(np.abs(hidden - ref[f"{case}/hidden"])[valid].max())
    report.add(name, f"fp32/{case}", stats)

    assert stats["max_abs"] < ATOL, stats
    assert stats["sampled_hf_logits_max_abs"] < ATOL, stats
    assert stats["top1_agreement"] == 1.0, stats


@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", models())
def test_window_edges_match_hf(name, report):
    """Test 3: on a 2048-token sequence (> 4 x local_attention), parity specifically at
    positions next to window edges: sequence ends (truncated windows) and every
    multiple of the half-window +- 1 (the blocked kernel's block seams)."""
    ref = reference(name)
    m = model(name)
    w = m.config.sliding_window
    length = ref["long/input_ids"].shape[1]
    assert length > 4 * m.config.local_attention
    edges = {p for k in range(0, length, w) for p in (k - 1, k, k + 1)}
    edges |= set(range(w + 2)) | set(range(length - w - 2, length))
    edges = np.array(sorted(p for p in edges if 0 <= p < length))

    logits, _ = run(name, "long")
    ours = logits[0, edges]
    theirs = reference_logits(name, "long")[0, edges]
    max_abs = float(np.abs(ours - theirs).max())
    top1 = float((ours.argmax(-1) == ref["long/top1"][0, edges]).mean())
    report.add(name, "fp32/window_edges", {"max_abs": max_abs, "top1_agreement": top1, "positions": len(edges)})
    assert max_abs < ATOL
    assert top1 == 1.0


@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", models())
@pytest.mark.parametrize("case", CASES)
def test_bf16_vs_fp32_reference(name, case, report):
    """Test 7: BF16 compute against the FP32 HF reference. No threshold; numbers go to the report."""
    ref = reference(name)
    logits, _ = run(name, case, dtype="bfloat16")
    stats = compare(logits, reference_logits(name, case), ref[f"{case}/top1"], ref[f"{case}/attention_mask"])
    report.add(name, f"bf16/{case}", stats)
    assert np.isfinite(logits).all()

"""Tests 1, 3 (HF parity at window edges), 4 and 7: logits vs HF transformers FP32 CPU eager."""

import mlx.core as mx
import numpy as np
import pytest

from helpers import CASES, compare, model, models, reference, reference_logits

ATOL = 1e-3


def run(name: str, case: str, dtype: str = "float32") -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    ref = reference(name)
    ids, mask = ref[f"{case}/input_ids"], ref[f"{case}/attention_mask"]
    m = model(name, dtype)
    # Pass the mask only for padded batches, as a user would.
    attn = mx.array(mask) if not mask.all() else None
    if m.config.is_decoder:
        hidden = m.hidden_states(mx.array(ids), attn)
    else:
        hidden = m.encode(mx.array(ids), attn)
    logits = m.logits(hidden)
    return np.array(logits.astype(mx.float32)), np.array(hidden.astype(mx.float32))


@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", models())
@pytest.mark.parametrize("case", CASES)
def test_fp32_logits_match_hf(name, case, report):
    """Tests 1 (encoders) and 4 (decoders): max abs diff < 1e-3 and 100% top-1 on every real position."""
    ref = reference(name)
    mask = ref[f"{case}/attention_mask"]
    logits, hidden = run(name, case)
    stats = compare(logits, reference_logits(name, case), ref[f"{case}/top1"], mask)

    pos = ref[f"{case}/sample_pos"]
    stats["sampled_hf_logits_max_abs"] = float(np.abs(logits[pos[:, 0], pos[:, 1]] - ref[f"{case}/sample_logits"]).max())
    valid = mask.astype(bool)
    stats["hidden_max_abs"] = float(np.abs(hidden - ref[f"{case}/hidden"])[valid].max())
    report.add(name, f"fp32/{case}", stats)

    assert stats["max_abs"] < ATOL, stats
    assert stats["sampled_hf_logits_max_abs"] < ATOL, stats
    assert stats["top1_agreement"] == 1.0, stats


@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", models())
def test_window_edges_match_hf(name, report):
    """Test 3: on a 2048-token sequence (> 4 x local_attention), parity specifically at
    positions next to window edges: sequence ends (truncated windows) and every
    multiple of the half-window +- 1 (the blocked kernel's block seams)."""
    ref = reference(name)
    m = model(name)
    w = m.config.sliding_window
    length = ref["long/input_ids"].shape[1]
    assert length > 4 * m.config.local_attention
    edges = {p for k in range(0, length, w) for p in (k - 1, k, k + 1)}
    edges |= set(range(w + 2)) | set(range(length - w - 2, length))
    edges = np.array(sorted(p for p in edges if 0 <= p < length))

    logits, _ = run(name, "long")
    ours = logits[0, edges]
    theirs = reference_logits(name, "long")[0, edges]
    max_abs = float(np.abs(ours - theirs).max())
    top1 = float((ours.argmax(-1) == ref["long/top1"][0, edges]).mean())
    report.add(name, "fp32/window_edges", {"max_abs": max_abs, "top1_agreement": top1, "positions": len(edges)})
    assert max_abs < ATOL
    assert top1 == 1.0


@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", models())
@pytest.mark.parametrize("case", CASES)
def test_bf16_vs_fp32_reference(name, case, report):
    """Test 7: BF16 compute against the FP32 HF reference. No threshold; numbers go to the report."""
    ref = reference(name)
    logits, _ = run(name, case, dtype="bfloat16")
    stats = compare(logits, reference_logits(name, case), ref[f"{case}/top1"], ref[f"{case}/attention_mask"])
    report.add(name, f"bf16/{case}", stats)
    assert np.isfinite(logits).all()
